clue.text: Old flier with RAF. a combination to invite disaster

indicators.note: a combination is a new mixing together, so these letters are combined into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A veteran airman teams up with the RAF in a pairing doomed to go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination' is the anagram signal: the letters of OLD, FLIER, RAF and A are rearranged. 'Old flier' looks like one phrase for a veteran pilot, but OLD is fodder on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave in a way that is bound to bring trouble upon yourself.

clue.text: Thorough search revealing strange old magician

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a mage is an archaic word for a wizard

explanation.surface: A close investigation uncovers an eccentric elderly conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: To root through things looking for something is to make a thorough, untidy search.

clue.text: Contributor has name exhibited in entrance

indicators.note: something exhibited in a place is shown inside it, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A benefactor's name is displayed in the doorway of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A giver who contributes money or blood to a cause is called by this word.

clue.text: Over a long period, better headgear developed for fighter

parts.note: for can mean over a stretch of time, as in 'for years'
an age is a long period of time
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Over many years, an improved helmet has been designed for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft peaked military cap worn by soldiers off the battlefield.

clue.text: Fret about deal, perhaps

parts.note: re means about or concerning
deal is a softwood timber, and pine is an example of it

explanation.surface: Someone worries anxiously over a business arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' reads as a bargain, but here it is the timber; 'perhaps' marks pine as one example of deal wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to pine, mope or be discontented, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Dance with colour sergeant, say

parts.note: flame is an orange-red colour
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, abbreviated NCO

explanation.surface: Someone takes to the dance floor with the regiment's colour sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colour sergeant' looks like one army rank, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate Spanish dance from Andalusia goes by this name.

clue.text: In general, when to rent

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, signalled by the opening preposition

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A question about the usual time for letting a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as the phrase meaning usually; split, 'In' is the container signal and 'general' is LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To let or hire property under contract for a set period is to take it on this kind of agreement.

clue.text: Wild pubs and clubs one goes into

indicators.note: a piece that goes into another enters it, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a pub is a bar, so pubs, being more than one, gives two bars
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Rowdy drinking dens and nightclubs that someone frequents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pubs' gives BAR twice; 'one goes into' places I between that pair and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage, uncivilised and untamed behaviour can be described with this adjective.

clue.text: Boss put over satellite workshop

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put over another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A manager is placed in charge of a satellite branch workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not a manager but a stud, the raised knob; 'satellite' is not a branch office but Jupiter's moon.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsman's working room is a studio.

clue.text: Hallway, so to speak

parts.note: split, the word is 'hall' and 'way': a country hall is a ... house, and a way is a manner, which sounds just like it

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Hallway' as two words: a hall in the sense of a country house, and 'way', meaning manner, which 'so to speak' says is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A country hall is a lord's estate house, the manor house.

clue.text: Be instrumental in entertainment in several pieces

parts.note: a play is a theatrical entertainment
apart means broken into pieces

explanation.surface: A musician helps out at a show performed in sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' suggests music, but here it means helping to bring something about.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute significantly to an outcome is to have a role in it.

clue.text: Go back into island church, showing pride

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: back means the short word go is read in reverse

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone returns to an island church, proudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back' reads as an instruction to return, but 'back' is the reversal signal and 'into' the container signal; Arran is a Scottish island, and 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughtiness and an inflated sense of one's own importance are a form of pride.

clue.text: Plant doctor found in river going West

indicators.note: found in means one piece is located inside another
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the river's name is reversed

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: A doctor is discovered by a westward-flowing river, among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going West' turns the river backwards, as an across clue reads right to left; 'found in' puts MB inside. 'Plant' is a verb here, to fix firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to set it firmly into a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Wipe away some decaff etc overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the run of letters taken from the phrase is read backwards
some means just part of the phrase decaff etc is taken

explanation.surface: Someone mops up spilt decaf coffee and other upset drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ECAFFE from 'decaff etc', and 'overturned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out or erase something is to wipe it away.

clue.text: Part of dissident group round king

indicators.note: round means the group's word goes around the other letter

parts.note: a faction is a breakaway dissenting group within a party
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A section of a rebel movement surrounds their monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of a whole, a fragment, is what this word means.

clue.text: Possible sequence of events as one car is crashed

indicators.note: a crashed car is smashed out of shape, so these letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A hypothetical chain of events when a car crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' signals an anagram of ONE CAR IS; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A projected outline of how things might unfold is a scenario.

clue.text: With old hipbone being broken, a fear of new

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly patient with a broken hip, afraid of new things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broken' rearranges O and HIPBONE; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek roots mean dread of novelty, an aversion to anything unfamiliar.

clue.text: Abandon craft — it's practical

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft, a type of craft
''tis on' means it is on, that is, feasible or practicable

explanation.surface: Someone decides to ditch a vessel because that is the sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's practical' gives 'TIS ON: 'tis is the old contraction of it is, and 'on' means achievable.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw overboard or discard is to abandon.

clue.text: Rascal observed embracing friend quietly

indicators.note: embracing means one word holds the others within its arms

parts.note: seen means observed
a pal is a friend
p (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A rogue is spotted hugging a mate on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: SPALPEEN is an Irish word for a rascal or worthless fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish term for a scamp or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Careless agent given chop internally

indicators.note: internally means the chopping word sits inside the agent word

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
to lop is to chop off

explanation.surface: A clumsy secret agent is struck a blow inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Messy, slapdash work done without care is described this way.

clue.text: Auntie entering ring towards wild animal

indicators.note: entering means the ring letter goes inside the broadcaster's letters

parts.note: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC, the national broadcaster
O is ring-shaped
at can mean towards, as in 'throw it at me'

explanation.surface: An aunt walks into a circus ring near a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, affectionately nicknamed for its once old-fashioned manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobcat is a North American lynx, a wild cat.

clue.text: Soldiers drank rum — from this?

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the following word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops knocked back spirits — what were they drinking from?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the anagram signal for DRANK. The whole clue is the definition: a beer mug soldiers might drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinking mug, often pewter with a handle, used for beer.

clue.text: American ship brought in to pick up a part to be inserted

indicators.note: brought in to means placed inside the other word

parts.note: to get something is to pick it up
USS stands for United States Ship, the prefix of American naval vessels

explanation.surface: A US vessel arrives to collect a component for fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' is the container GET here, not a verb about collecting the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusset is a triangular piece of cloth inserted into a garment to strengthen or enlarge it.

clue.text: Best fête champêtre?

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to beat or surpass them
a fête champêtre is a French phrase for an open-air rural party; the question mark warns the reading is playful

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'do' is British for a party, so an outdoor party becomes an OUT DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or beat someone is to best them.

clue.text: He has finally to bow down before Caesar

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A man ultimately has to bow down before the Roman emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of each of TO, BOW, DOWN, BEFORE and CAESAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is one who has something, which is exactly this person.

clue.text: As result of this, try to land

definitions.text: As result of this, try to land

parts.words: As result of this, try to land
parts.note: in rugby, grounding the ball over the line earns a try; and for an aircraft, coming to land means touching the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'try' reads as attempt, but it is the rugby score that results from grounding the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the grounding of the ball scores a try, and an aircraft landing makes the same contact with the ground.

clue.text: Old judge to make a speech

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An elderly magistrate rises to deliver an address.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak formally or pompously, as if giving an oration.

clue.text: Forecast numbers I included in short programmes

indicators.note: included in means these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: progs is a shortened form of programmes

explanation.surface: A forecast of figures is featured in brief broadcasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical forecast of how a disease will progress is a prognosis.

clue.text: Black and white are used in title

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils and in chess
wan means pale or white-faced
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Monochrome is employed in a heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not the verb but the metric unit of 100 square metres; 'and' and 'used in' are links. A bwana is a respectful title meaning master in Swahili.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa this Swahili form of address means master or sir, used before a name.

clue.text: A Brit had gone out to precipitate a crisis

indicators.note: out means the letters go out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British person leaving causes matters to come to a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of A BRIT HAD GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to force matters to a decisive point, like a boil coming to a head.
